features.summary: The platform decoder and encoder backends were cleaned up and made more robust, including safer Apple VideoToolbox and Windows Media Foundation state handling, removal of obsolete audio decoder types, and an FFmpeg resource-leak fix. On Linux, ffvpx now gains Vulkan support and better compatibility with older system FFmpeg versions, with Vulkan device caching improving efficiency. These changes make hardware-accelerated media playback and encoding more reliable across operating systems.

Unused decoder debugging code and obsolete mixed-content telemetry were removed, while a C++ destructor was moved for compatibility; most of this is maintenance with no visible change.

Related event-dispatch changes make initialization and finalization of the HTML media element's user-agent shadow DOM safer when scripts could run, reducing timing and re-entrancy risks without changing the intended media controls.

features.summary: New tests improve privacy and robustness checks: there’s a test ensuring media load-error messages are properly redacted across redirects (protecting error details), a crashtest for multichannel audio through the SoundTouch time-stretcher (audio processing stability), and adjusted visual-test tolerances for macOS rendering differences. These help prevent regressions in error handling, audio processing, and visual rendering across platforms.

features.summary: Gecko Media Plugins (GMP), Firefox's framework for integrated media plugins such as DRM components, received more reliable task handling. The macOS crash reporter no longer relies on a fragile thread-ID workaround, improving plugin startup and crash diagnostics.

patches.subject: Preserve HDR metadata in planar YUV image copies

patches.author: Andrew Osmond
patches.subject: Harden remote encoding state machine in RemoteMediaDataEncoderParent.

features.summary: Media IPC now preserves HDR metadata when planar YUV video frames are copied between processes, so the compositor can retain the information needed for correct brightness and color. The remote media encoder state machine was also hardened to handle unusual transitions more safely, improving reliability for out-of-process encoding.

patches.subject: Clear SoundTouch state when discarding future audio

features.summary: Audio playback now clears SoundTouch's time-stretching state when future audio is discarded, preventing old timing data from affecting newly queued sound. Tests also verify SoundTouch's destination-buffer limits through the audio decoder track, helping avoid glitches when playback seeks or is resynchronized.

features.label: WebCodecs

patches.author: Randell Jesup
patches.subject: Don't cancel the ImageDecoder read request from cycle-collection unlink

features.summary: ImageDecoder and WebCodecs teardown logic was adjusted to avoid canceling read requests during cycle-collection and to remove unsafe script-execution boundaries during teardown. In practice this stabilizes the WebCodecs/ImageDecoder path (the browser API for low-level image and video frame decoding) so background garbage collection doesn’t unexpectedly abort or corrupt in-progress image reads.

patches.author: Exploding-Joysticks
patches.subject: Remove the media.eme.encrypted-media-encryption-scheme.enabled pref

features.summary: Firefox removed the preference controlling the encrypted-media encryption-scheme feature in Encrypted Media Extensions (EME), the web API used for DRM-protected video and audio. The setting is no longer needed, simplifying configuration while leaving supported DRM playback behavior unchanged.

features.label: Media Source Extensions (MSE)

patches.author: az
patches.subject: Part 2: Add tests for the WebM init segment boundary across back to back init segments.

features.summary: Media Source Extensions (MSE), which lets web pages stream media in chunks, gained tests for WebM initialization segments placed back to back. The coverage ensures Firefox recognizes each segment boundary correctly, helping streaming players avoid malformed transitions when switching or appending media.

features.label: Web Audio

patches.author: Matthew Gregan
patches.subject: Reorder multichannel Vorbis channels in ffvpx's libvorbis decoder wrapper.

features.summary: The Web Audio decoding path now reorders channels for multichannel Vorbis audio in the ffvpx/libvorbis wrapper. This aligns the decoded channel layout with what Firefox and web content expect, so surround sound is less likely to come out of the wrong speakers.

features.label: WebM

patches.author: az
patches.subject: Part 1: Stop the WebM init segment boundary running into a following init segment.

features.summary: WebM media parsing was corrected so the boundary marking the end of one initialization segment cannot run into a following initialization segment. This matters for Media Source Extensions (MSE) streaming, where clear init-segment boundaries help players append consecutive WebM headers reliably.

features.summary: Caption and WebVTT event dispatching helpers were marked for correct script-run safety, aligning them with the same MOZ_CAN_RUN_SCRIPT annotations used elsewhere. This ensures subtitle/caption event callbacks run in a safe, well-defined context and reduces subtle stability or security issues in the captions pipeline.

features.summary: Firefox substantially improved platform media acceleration across Linux, Windows, Android, and macOS. Linux Vulkan Video support now covers more hardware and FFmpeg configurations, caches devices and codec capabilities, fails cleanly when required functions are unavailable, and avoids unsupported H.264 cases; Windows Media Foundation avoids risky realtime VPX hardware encoding and rejects invalid odd-width inputs; Apple VideoToolbox handles planar, mapped, and NVImage frames more safely.
